title: Construct String from Binary Tree
notes:
Task: Serialize a binary tree as a string using each node value and parentheses around child representations, omitting unnecessary empty parentheses but preserving a right child when needed.
Idea: Serialize the left child when present; if a right child exists without a left child, emit an empty left pair before the right representation.
Invariant: The traversal or stored state summarizes the portion of the input already processed.
Edge cases: root=[1,2,3,4] -> "1(2(4))(3)"
complexity_reason: Each node is serialized once; recursion follows tree height.

title: Find Duplicate File in System
notes:
Task: Given directory descriptions containing file names and contents, return groups of full file paths that share identical contents.
Idea: Parse each file entry, map its content to the full path, and return only groups containing at least two paths.
Invariant: The traversal or stored state summarizes the portion of the input already processed.
Edge cases: paths=["root/a 1.txt(ab) 2.txt(cd)","root/b 3.txt(ab)"] -> [["root/a/1.txt","root/b/3.txt"]]
complexity_reason: Each file entry is parsed once and stored under its content.

title: Valid Triangle Number
approach_name: Sort and count with two pointers
notes:
Task: Count triples of array elements that can form the side lengths of a non-degenerate triangle.
Idea: After sorting, for each largest side use two pointers to count pairs whose sum is greater than it.
Invariant: The traversal or stored state summarizes the portion of the input already processed.
Edge cases: nums=[2,2,3,4] -> 3
complexity_reason: For each largest side, two pointers count valid smaller-side pairs.

title: Merge Two Binary Trees
notes:
Task: Merge two binary trees by adding values where both nodes exist; where only one node exists, keep that node and its subtree.
Idea: Recursively add overlapping node values and merge corresponding left and right children.
Invariant: The traversal or stored state summarizes the portion of the input already processed.
Edge cases: root1=[1,3,2,5], root2=[2,1,3,null,4,null,7] -> root=[3,4,5,5,4,null,7]
complexity_reason: Only overlapping nodes require a merge; unmatched subtrees are reused.

title: Task Scheduler
notes:
Task: Schedule tasks represented by uppercase letters with a cooldown of n intervals between identical tasks; return the minimum total intervals including idle time.
Idea: The most frequent task determines a frame of (maxFrequency-1)*(n+1), extended by the number of tasks tied for maximum frequency; the answer cannot be shorter than the task count.
Invariant: The traversal or stored state summarizes the portion of the input already processed.
Edge cases: tasks=[A,A,A,B,B,B], n=2 -> 8
complexity_reason: Task frequencies determine the frame lower bound.

title: Add One Row to Tree
approach_name: Insert a row at requested depth
notes:
Task: Insert a row of nodes with value val at the given depth, attaching old left subtrees as new left children and old right subtrees as new right children.
Idea: For depth one create a new root; otherwise find nodes at depth-1 and insert two children around their existing subtrees.
Invariant: The traversal or stored state summarizes the portion of the input already processed.
Edge cases: root=[4,2,6,3,1,5], val=1, depth=2 -> [4,1,1,2,null,null,6,3,1,5]
complexity_reason: The traversal reaches the parent level and wraps existing child subtrees.

title: Maximum Product of Three Numbers
notes:
Task: Return the maximum product obtainable from any three numbers in an integer array.
Idea: The best product is either the product of the three largest values or the two most negative values times the largest value.
Invariant: The traversal or stored state summarizes the portion of the input already processed.
Edge cases: nums=[-1,-2,-3] -> -6
complexity_reason: The optimum uses either the three largest or two smallest and the largest.

title: Average of Levels in Binary Tree
notes:
Task: Return the average value of nodes at each depth of a binary tree, from root to deepest level.
Idea: Process one BFS level at a time, sum its node values, and divide by the level size.
Invariant: The traversal or stored state summarizes the portion of the input already processed.
Edge cases: root=[3,9,20,null,null,15,7] -> [3.0,14.5,11.0]
complexity_reason: Each node is processed once and the queue holds a level frontier.

title: Maximum Average Subarray I
notes:
Task: Find the maximum average among all contiguous subarrays of length k.
Idea: Compute the first window sum and update it by adding the incoming value and removing the outgoing value.
Invariant: The traversal or stored state summarizes the portion of the input already processed.
Edge cases: nums=[1,12,-5,-6,50,3], k=4 -> 12.75
complexity_reason: Each window update adds one value and removes one value.

title: Set Mismatch
notes:
Task: An array should contain each integer from 1 through n once, but one value is duplicated and another is missing; return [duplicate, missing].
Idea: Track seen values to identify the duplicate, then find the value in 1..n that never appeared.
Invariant: The traversal or stored state summarizes the portion of the input already processed.
Edge cases: nums=[1,2,2,4] -> [2,3]
complexity_reason: A set or boolean array identifies the duplicate and missing values.
